PRIME MINISTER, DEPUTY PRIME MINISTER, Pham Gia Tuc REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ORGANIZATION, MANAGEMENT STAFF AND TRAINING DOCUMENT SYSTEM OF THE FACILITY TRAINING AND PROFESSIONAL TRAINING OF AVIATION STAFF (Attached to Decree No. 221/2026/ND-CP June 22, 2026 of the Government) I. Requirements on organizational structure and staff managing training and coaching work of training and coaching establishments: 1. Training facilities must designate a person responsible for ensuring compliance with the requirements applicable to the training facility. 2. Training and coaching establishments must arrange enough personnel to meet the professional and capacity requirements for each job position in terms of management, developing training programs, conducting training and inspection; operate and maintain simulated training equipment or aircraft for training; Organize the implementation, supervision, inspection, testing and control of training and coaching activities according to regulations of the Minister of Construction and ensure compliance with the approved training scope. 3. The training facility must ensure that its human resources are trained according to the internal training program specified in the training document system of the training facility. II. Requirements for the training and coaching document system of the training facility: The documentation system of the Aviation Personnel Training Facility may include one or more documents but must include at least the following contents: 1. Organizational structure, standards, functions and tasks of personnel positions. 2. Document system structure; 3. Roles, functions, tasks, and scope of training of training and coaching establishments. 4. Training and coaching policies and procedures. 5. Detailed programs, textbooks, training courses, and training appropriate to the approved training scope. 6. Quality assurance system, including the process of controlling training records and issuing certificates of course completion. 7. Safety management system as prescribed in Article 29 of this Decree. 8. Policies and procedures to calculate the maximum number of students that the organization can train at the same time. 9. Minimum standards for each personnel position according to regulations. 10. Record keeping processes, systems and methods. 11. Information about each location of the training facility. 12. List and features of equipment at each location for each training course. 13. List of training courses conducted at each location. FACILITY REQUIREMENTS TRAINING FACILITIES, PROFESSIONAL TRAINING FOR AVIATION STAFF (Attached to Decree No. 221/2026/ND-CP June 22, 2026 of the Government) I. General requirements for classrooms and discussion rooms Aviation staff training and professional training facilities must ensure that classrooms and discussion rooms meet the following regulations: 1. Have adequate lighting, air conditioning and ventilation systems suitable to the local climate, hygiene and health. 2. Do not distract students from outside activities, flight operations and maintenance operations at the airport. 3. Must be equipped with tables and chairs for students and teachers; Presentation and audio-visual equipment suitable for the type of training. 4. Have a minimum area of ​​1.5 m2 per student for theory classes and a minimum of 3 m2 for practical classes. II. Requirements for training facilities and professional training for aviation staff in the field of airport operations: 1. Infrastructure and equipment for professional practice training must meet the following minimum requirements: a) For professional practice training for vehicle drivers operating at the airport, and operating aviation equipment at the airport: a1) Have a practice area to ensure the painting of signals and signs according to regulations on painting signals and signs on aircraft aprons in accordance with the professional skills being trained and trained; a2) Have equipment and means of practice suitable to the professional skills being trained and trained; a3) Have a mock-up model of aircraft parts corresponding to the type of equipment, practice facilities with direct access to the aircraft and trained professional skills. b) For practical training of ground handling staff serving flights: b1) Have a practice area suitable for professional practice and training; b2) Have a system of simulated equipment and software to guide practice corresponding to the professional skills being trained and coached; b3) Have a mock-up model of aircraft parts corresponding to the professional skills being trained. c) For practical training of rescue and firefighting personnel: have equipment and facilities for rescue and firefighting operations, ensuring realistic simulation of fire, high temperature and pressure, reduced visibility, specifically as follows: c1) Fire area to create a fire environment, serving rescue and firefighting practices, using equipment and chemicals used to fight aircraft fires in aircraft fire situations; c2) The fire engine operating area surrounds the fire area, is large enough in size and ensures a structure for fire engines to access and rescue and firefighting personnel to perform rescue and firefighting activities; c3) The aircraft model has a structure, shape, and size similar to a typical aircraft operating commercially at the airport; The model can be installed permanently or mobilely and includes external (wings, wheels and tires, engine...) and internal (passenger compartment, passenger seats...); c4) Control area for operators to control and control hypothetical fire situations in the fire area. Control can be programmed automatically or performed by the operator to create a situation; c5) Support systems include: fuel supply system, water supply and recovery system, electrical system. 2. Training establishments are allowed to use works, infrastructure, facilities, and equipment at airports to serve practical training of aviation staff on the basis of agreement with airport operators and aviation service businesses and ensure that they meet the requirements for facilities according to regulations. III. Requirements for facilities of the training and professional training facility for aviation staff in the field of flight operations assurance: 1. For training and coaching of air traffic controllers: Training and coaching facilities must ensure that there is at least 01 simulation training device suitable for the training and coaching program. Simulation training equipment must meet the following requirements: a) Ensure operational features, functions and technical characteristics are consistent with the training scope of the facility; b) Be maintained to ensure the reliability of operational features, functions and other technical characteristics required during the qualification process; Have a backup plan to replace or fix immediately so as not to interrupt the training program; c) Modified and updated to always be consistent with airspace organization, airport configuration, aircraft type, systems, and operational features; d) Check daily operating functions and before being put into use for training; d) Have a technical diary for teachers and assessors to record any discrepancies and failures that arise after each training lesson. 2. For training and professional training of technical staff to ensure flight operations: Must have and maintain the following training equipment appropriate to the scope of training and coaching: a) Equipment, models, training tools and supplies, hardware parts and control software (if necessary) in accordance with the content of the training program; b) Able to access or use for practical purposes the actual equipment system of the type of equipment to ensure flight operations; In case there is no actual equipment system, there must be simulated training equipment or equivalent simulation approved by the Vietnam Aviation Administration; c) Ensure the number of equipment, models, and training materials meets the ratio of no more than 08 students per device or model at the same time; d) Equipment specified in Point b of this Clause, if it has been discontinued or previously damaged, must be maintained or repaired so that it can be used for training purposes and is not required to meet actual operating standards. 3. For training and professional training of aviation meteorological staff: a) Have equipment and information and data systems suitable to the content of training and professional training programs; b) Able to access or use for practical purposes a real meteorological equipment system; c) Equipment specified in Point b of this Clause, if it has been discontinued or previously damaged, must be maintained or repaired so that it can be used for training purposes and is not required to meet actual operating standards. 4. For training and professional training of flight procedure design staff and civil aviation maps and diagrams: a) Have procedures for building and designing flight procedures, maps and aeronautical diagrams; b) Have an aviation map system, information system, data and equipment to serve the design of flight procedures, construction of maps and aviation diagrams in accordance with the content of training and coaching programs. 5. For training and professional training of aviation search and rescue staff: a) Have a map system and calculation tool, equipped with a map system (or digital map), calculation support software or specialized tables to help students practice identifying priority areas and calculating the probability of searching and detecting targets based on coordinates and wind direction data. b) Able to access or use for practical purposes actual search and rescue equipment systems, including: b1) Emergency information and data processing system: Air traffic service telegram processing system for distress reporting and Cospas-Sarsat emergency signal transceiver system; b2) Communication and storage system: Radio and satellite communication system for communication, recording and storage system for recording incident logs and analyzing and commenting on executive conversations; b3) Field equipment (Search and rescue command vehicle, black box detector and rescue equipment, tent deployment, UAV equipment control). 6. For training and professional training of aviation communication equipment operators, aviation information staff, flight plan procedure support staff and other types of flight operations assurance staff not included in items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 above: a) Have an information and data system consistent with the content of training and professional training programs; b) Have enough practice equipment consistent with the content of the training and professional training program. 7. Training facilities must ensure that training equipment used for training must be inspected and evaluated to meet the conditions according to the approved training program. 8. Training facilities must establish a document and record storage system with approved content within the scope of training. 9. Training establishments are allowed to use infrastructure, facilities, and equipment at flight operations assurance service providers and aviation service businesses to serve the training and practical training of aviation staff in the field of flight operations assurance on the basis of agreement with flight operations assurance service enterprises and aviation service businesses. IV. Requirements for facilities of training and professional training facilities for aviation staff in the field of aircraft and aircraft operations 1. Training facilities must maintain, operate and fully arrange training facilities and equipment to ensure technical requirements consistent with the approved training scope. The Minister of Construction regulates technical requirements for equipment serving training and coaching activities. 2. When a training facility rents facilities and equipment for training, it must prove that the training facility has the right to access and use the facilities, equipment and documents necessary to organize approved training courses. 3. Training facilities must ensure that training equipment used for training must be inspected and evaluated to meet the conditions according to the approved training program. 4. Training facilities must establish a document and record storage system with approved contents within the scope of training. 5. Simulator training equipment used for training courses must be approved by the Vietnam Aviation Administration. 6. Aircraft used for training purposes to issue a pilot license must be maintained according to regulations on aircraft maintenance. REQUIREMENTS FOR TEACHERS AT TRAINING FACILITIES, PROFESSIONAL TRAINING FOR AVIATION STAFF (Attached to Decree No. 221/2026/ND-CP June 22, 2026 of the Government) I. Requirements for teachers at training facilities and professional training for aviation staff in the field of airport operations: 1. Teachers teaching general knowledge of civil aviation must have a certificate of general knowledge of civil aviation. 2. Teachers teach professional skills: a) Teachers teaching theory must have a professional certificate corresponding to the subject taught; b) Practical teachers are aviation employees with professional certificates corresponding to the subjects taught; c) Professional teachers must have at least 5 years of experience working in a professional field related to the subject taught. 3. Aviation staff training and professional training establishments must have enough theoretical and practical teachers to ensure that each specialized aviation subject must have at least 01 teacher teaching. 4. Training and coaching establishments can maintain the form of professional teachers, part-time teachers, and guest lecturers specializing in aviation. The number of guest lecturers in aviation majors of the training and coaching establishment must not be greater than 50% of the number of specialized aviation teachers of the training establishment. II. Requirements for teachers at training facilities and professional training for aviation staff in the field of flight operations assurance 1. General requirements a) Theory and practice teachers conduct training and coaching to issue, renew, and restore licenses, professional certificates, and ratings for air traffic controllers; Employees who operate aviation communication equipment must be licensed and rated by the Vietnam Aviation Administration according to the provisions of Article 42 of this Decree. b) Theoretical and practical teachers who conduct training and coaching for staff in the field of flight operations assurance who are not subject to licensing or rating must have their internal capacity assessed and confirmed by the aviation staff training facility and assigned to perform teacher duties in writing. c) Aviation staff training and professional training establishments must have enough theoretical and practical teachers to ensure that each specialized aviation subject must have at least 01 teacher teaching. d) Training and coaching establishments can maintain the form of professional teachers, part-time teachers, and guest lecturers specializing in aviation. The number of guest lecturers in aviation majors of the training and coaching establishment must not be greater than 50% of the number of specialized aviation teachers of the training establishment. 2. Theory teacher standards: Meet the general regulations in Article 50 of this Decree, ensuring subject-related knowledge is fully updated and applied in practice. 3. General standards for practicing teachers: a) Meet the general regulations in Article 50 of this Decree; b) Have the capacity, professional qualifications, and practical exploitation experience consistent with the content of practical training; c) Have knowledge of competency-based training, coaching and assessment methods; d) Demonstrate proficiency in modeling, monitoring, supervising and evaluating student skills. d) Must participate in periodic training courses and have teaching capacity re-evaluated periodically with a cycle of no more than 24 months. e) Re-entry training: Practicing teachers who do not maintain their training must receive re-entry training. 4. Teachers practicing training on the simulation system (Simulator Instructor) must meet the following conditions: a) Complete a training course on operating simulation training equipment; b) Correctly operate control systems and equipment of simulation training equipment, environmental setup tables, weather conditions, and assume system and equipment failures; c) Understand the technical limitations and limitations of the system compared to the actual operating environment; d) Have skills in setting up scenarios and effectively using specific techniques of the simulation system (such as pausing, replaying, changing tempo, assuming emergency situations) to optimize analysis, feedback, and commentary for students; d) Experience requirements: Have at least two years of experience for the rating they will be teaching, and have current mining knowledge. 5. Teachers practicing training air traffic controllers at their working positions must meet the following conditions: a) Have a valid air traffic controller license and rating, suitable for the scope of instruction and training at the working position; b) Have confirmation of exploitation at the unit or work location where OJT is performed; c) Complete the training program, training teachers to practice at work positions for air traffic controllers according to the competency-based training and assessment (CBTA) method by training and coaching facilities recognized by ICAO or the Civil Aviation Authority of Vietnam; d) Experience requirements: d1) Have held an air traffic controller rating in which they will participate in teaching for at least two years; d2) Have a valid air traffic controller rating at the facility where the training will be conducted. d) Complete periodic training content, skills tests and maintain current experience in accordance with requirements for air traffic controllers. 6. Teachers practice on-the-job training (OJTI) for aviation communications equipment operators who meet the following conditions: a) Have practical experience in working at a working position that meets the regulations of the ANS service provider; b) Complete the on-the-job training (OJTI) teacher training course. III. Requirements for teachers at training facilities and professional training for aviation staff in the field of aircraft and aircraft operations: 1. Theory teachers and practical teachers at training and professional training facilities for aviation staff in the field of aircraft and aircraft operations must be licensed, rated or have a professional certificate by the Vietnam Aviation Administration as prescribed in Article 42 of this Decree. 2. Before performing teaching duties, teachers must be trained according to the internal training program for teachers in the Documentation System of the Aviation Personnel Professional Training and Training Facility. 3. The Minister of Construction regulates teacher positions; training, coaching, testing, assessment and capacity maintenance programs; Rights and responsibilities of teachers at aviation staff training and professional training establishments. LIST OF SERIOUS INCIDENTS (Attached to Decree No. 221/2026/ND-CP June 22, 2026 of the Government) 1. Competent state agencies determine that an aviation safety incident is called a serious incident according to the following principles: a) Carry out incident-based risk analysis to evaluate whether or not an accident scenario can occur based on the layers of defense that separate the boundary between incident and accident; b) Defense layers can be aircraft technology, flight crew capacity, standard procedures, capacity of the air traffic controller system, aircraft backup system, aircraft design principles or conditions and characteristics that are barriers to help incidents not lead to accidents; c) In case an accident is just lucky to not happen or the incident occurs with limited defenses and there is a high risk of an accident, the incident is determined to be a serious incident. 2. The list of incidents initially classified as serious incidents is as follows: a) Aircraft that are close to colliding with each other must take avoidance actions to avoid collision or dangerous situations; Actual separation between aircraft is less than 50% of the minimum separation value; b) Aircraft collide with each other or collide with vehicles, ground equipment or obstacles but this is not an accident; c) Operating the aircraft into a terrain area that exceeds the minimum safety limit and must take actions to avoid it. Cancel takeoff on closed takeoff and landing runways; Take-off and landing runways are being occupied; on the taxiway or not on the designated takeoff or landing runway; d) Taking off on closed takeoff and landing runways; Take-off and landing runways are being occupied; on the taxiway or not on the designated takeoff or landing runway; d) Landing or attempting to land on closed or occupied take-off or landing runways, undesignated take-off or landing runways or unintended locations such as roads; e) Landing beyond the takeoff or landing runway or exiting the takeoff or landing runway; g) Damage leading to the aircraft not achieving expected performance during takeoff or initial climb; h) Fire or smoke in the cockpit, passenger compartment, cargo room or engine fire, even if extinguished with fire extinguishing agents; i) An emergency requires the crew to use emergency oxygen; k) Structural damage requiring major repair or engine separation but not serious enough to cause an accident; l) Multiple damages occur to one or more aircraft systems that seriously affect aircraft control; m) The pilot loses the ability to work while the aircraft is in flight: (1) For flights operated with one pilot; (2) For flights operated with multiple pilots where flight safety is affected by a significant increase in workload for the remaining crew members. n) Insufficient fuel forces the crew to declare an emergency; o) Aircraft nearly collide with each other, with vehicles or people on the takeoff and landing routes; p) System failures (including loss of power or thrust), unusual weather phenomena or aircraft operations beyond approved limits or situations that make it difficult to control the aircraft; q) Landing with the aircraft's undercarriage or wheels not released is not classified as an accident; r) Dragging during landing at the wing tip, engine or any other part of the aircraft that is not classified as an accident. 3. After investigating, verifying or evaluating the safety risks and consequences of the incident, the aviation authorities may change or supplement the classification of serious incidents for aviation incidents.
